B.issue: Deleting RestClientConfig removes the only wiring of TraceIdPropagationInterceptor, which survives as an orphaned @Component (plus its test and the cdp.tracing.header-name property) whose Javadoc still claims it adds x-cdp-request-id to every outbound RestClient/RestTemplate call - it now adds it to none, so the stated CDP tracing requirement is silently unenforced for any future outbound client (the 10s connect / 30s read timeouts went with it too).
B.fix: Finish the cleanup either way: delete TraceIdPropagationInterceptor, its test and the cdp.tracing.header-name property alongside RestClientConfig; or keep a minimal @Configuration exposing a RestClient.Builder bean with .requestInterceptor(traceIdInterceptor) and the timeouts, per best-practice section 17.

B.issue: Response shape contradicts docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml (committed in this same PR) on every property: locked Operator is snake_case with required crn, status enum and operator_type plus address_line_1/town/country/telephone; OperatorResponse emits camelCase addressLine1/townOrCity/countryCode/phone, a derived deleted boolean, and drops crn and operator_type entirely - so the PR ships two committed contract documents that disagree field-for-field
B.fix: Re-issue api-contract.locked.yaml to the ruled untyped camelCase model (or revert the record to the locked shape), and extend OperatorComplianceIT.apiDocsMatchTheCommittedArtifactAndTheLockedContract to diff components.schemas property names - today it only compares path set, HTTP methods and operationIds, so the schema divergence passes the gate the Javadoc claims it enforces

B.issue: countryCode reverses declared deviation D1 of the locked contract, which rules country is an MDM display-name string (e.g. 'United Kingdom'), NOT ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, and states reviewers must not silently 'fix' it; Address.java documents countryCode as ISO alpha-2 (cv-011), so this is a value-semantics change not just a rename - a consumer rendering the address gets 'GB' where the contract promises 'United Kingdom' and D1 records that no code-to-name conversion exists anywhere in the epic
B.fix: Either emit the MDM display name as country, or record the superseding ruling in api-contract.locked.yaml (replacing D1) and confirm the frontend/animals-backend consumers resolve alpha-2 to a display name before render

B.issue: No @Schema on the record or any component, so the committed docs/openapi/operators.yml renders OperatorResponse with zero field descriptions and no required list - all 14 fields generate as optional in consumer client SDKs even though 11 are guaranteed non-null by the compact constructor
B.fix: Add a class-level @Schema(description=...) and per-component @Schema(description=..., example=..., requiredMode=Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED) for the 11 guarded fields (leave addressLine2/county default), then regenerate the artifact with mvn verify -Dopenapi.generate=true

B.issue: The 11 compact-constructor null guards are new behaviour with no test: OperatorMapperTest covers field-by-field mapping, the derived deleted boolean and camelCase serialisation, but nothing asserts a null id/name/countryCode/organisationId/createdAt throws, so the documented 'fails loud' contract is unverified and a guard could be dropped silently
B.fix: Add a parameterised OperatorResponseTest asserting NullPointerException with the field name as message for each guarded component, and that addressLine2/county accept null

B.issue: The PR adds @EnableMongoAuditing here, which turns on @CreatedDate/@LastModifiedDate but NOT optimistic locking — Address has no @Version field, so OperatorService.update() and delete() are unguarded read-modify-write full-document save() calls (last-write-wins; a concurrent delete can be resurrected by an in-flight PUT). Corroborates the open cross-file finding on Address.java.
B.fix: Add a @Version Long field to Address so Spring Data emits a version-predicated update, and map the resulting OptimisticLockingFailureException to 409 in GlobalExceptionHandler (or switch update/delete to a targeted findAndModify with a status/version predicate instead of save()).

B.issue: Both the invalid-format warn (line 59) and the parse-failure error (line 77) log the raw httpProxy value; CDP proxy URLs are of the form http://user:password@host:port, so a malformed value (e.g. missing scheme) leaks proxy credentials into CloudWatch logs
B.fix: Log a redacted form only - strip userinfo before logging (e.g. httpProxy.replaceAll("//[^@/]+@", "//***@")), or log just the fact that parsing failed plus proxyUri.getHost()

B.issue: ProxySelector.of() builds a selector with no bypass list and http.nonProxyHosts/https.nonProxyHosts are never set, so once HTTP_PROXY is present every outbound HTTP call - including localhost targets such as the cdp.cloudwatch.endpoint default http://localhost:4566, actuator self-calls and any in-test WireMock stub - is forced through the proxy and will fail; the class Javadoc's claim that no bypass is needed only covers *.cdp-int.defra.cloud routing by the squid proxy, not loopback
B.fix: Set System.setProperty("http.nonProxyHosts", "localhost|127.*|[::1]|*.cdp-int.defra.cloud") (and the https equivalent) and use a ProxySelector implementation that honours it rather than the unconditional ProxySelector.of(...)

B.issue: configureProxy() has no effective test coverage: ProxyConfigIT gates every meaningful assertion on System.getenv("HTTP_PROXY") being set, which it never is in CI, so the tests degrade to assertThat(proxyConfig).isNotNull() and a literal assertThat(true).isTrue() - none of the four branches (blank, invalid host/port, parse failure, happy path) is exercised
B.fix: Extract the parsing into a package-private method taking the proxy URL as an argument and unit-test it directly, or drive the Spring context with @TestPropertySource(properties = "cdp.proxyUrl=http://localhost:3128") plus negative cases, so the branches are asserted without depending on the OS environment

B.issue: configureProxy() mutates JVM-global state (four System properties plus ProxySelector.setDefault) from @PostConstruct and never restores it; ProxyConfigIT's @AfterAll clears the system properties but not the default ProxySelector, so once any test context sets a proxy it stays set for every later test class in the same Surefire/Failsafe JVM
B.fix: Prefer configuring a ProxyConfiguration on the specific RestClient/HttpClient builder the service uses; if the global approach is kept for CDP parity, capture and restore the previous ProxySelector in the test and document the global mutation as a deliberate CDP requirement

B.issue: Any userinfo in the proxy URL (http://user:pass@host:port) is silently discarded - only host and port are propagated and no java.net.Authenticator is installed - so against an authenticated proxy every request fails with 407 and the logs say the proxy was configured successfully
B.fix: Read proxyUri.getUserInfo(); if present, install an Authenticator (and set jdk.http.auth.tunneling.disabledSchemes="" for HTTPS CONNECT), or log a warn that credentials in HTTP_PROXY are not supported so the failure mode is visible

B.issue: The no-proxy guard uses isEmpty() rather than isBlank(), so a whitespace-only HTTP_PROXY (easy to produce from a CDP env-var template) falls through to URI.create(" "), throws IllegalArgumentException and is reported as an ERROR instead of taking the benign 'no proxy configured' path
B.fix: Use if (httpProxy == null || httpProxy.isBlank()) and strip() the value before URI.create - modern-java.md prefers isBlank()/strip() over isEmpty()/trim()

B.issue: cdp.proxyUrl is injected with @Value onto a private field, which is the field-injection anti-pattern the Spring Boot guide bans (section 7: always constructor injection, never field injection); it also makes the class untestable without a Spring context, which is why ProxyConfigIT is reduced to null checks
B.fix: Take the value as a constructor parameter - public ProxyConfig(@Value("${cdp.proxyUrl}") String httpProxy) - and assign to a final field

B.issue: cert == null conflates 'no CDP cert configured' with 'cert configured but unparseable' (CertificateLoader.loadCustomCertificate swallows CertificateException and returns null), so a corrupt TRUSTSTORE_CDP_ROOT_CA boots successfully with the default JVM trust store only and fails later at Mongo/CDP TLS connect time instead of at startup
B.fix: Make CertificateLoader rethrow (e.g. IllegalStateException) when the cdp.certificate property is non-empty but fails to parse, or have it return an Optional plus a 'configured' flag so customSslContext() can fail fast; keep the silent path only for the genuinely-unset case

B.issue: log.info hardcodes 'initialized successfully with 1 custom certificate' on every path, including when createCombinedTrustManager returned the default-only trust manager because cert was null - operations see '1 custom certificate' precisely when zero were loaded, masking the degradation above
B.fix: Log the real outcome, e.g. move the message inside the branches or log 'custom certificates loaded: {}' with (cert == null ? 0 : 1)

B.issue: @Order(Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE) plus the class javadoc claim that it 'ensures the SSLContext is available before other beans (like MongoClient) are created' is untrue - @Order on a @Configuration class affects configuration-class ordering, not bean instantiation timing; ordering here is actually guaranteed by MongoConfig injecting TrustStoreConfiguration
B.fix: Drop the @Order annotation and the Ordered import, and correct the javadoc to say ordering comes from dependency injection

B.issue: CombinedTrustManager.checkServerTrusted/checkClientTrusted discard the default trust manager's CertificateException when falling through to the custom trust manager, so when both reject a chain only the custom CDP trust manager's (usually less informative) error surfaces and the real public-CA failure reason is lost
B.fix: Capture the first exception and attach it via addSuppressed on the exception thrown by the custom trust manager (or log it at debug) before rethrowing

B.issue: createCombinedTrustManager declares 'throws Exception' and customSslContext catches bare Exception, which trips Sonar java:S112 and also swallows unrelated runtime faults (NPE, bean-wiring errors) behind the misleading 'Cannot initialize SSL context' message
B.fix: Narrow to 'throws GeneralSecurityException, IOException' on the helper and catch the same specific types in customSslContext

B.issue: Class Javadoc names two triggers that never throw this exception: a missing identity header is rejected inside IdentityHeaderFilter (which writes problem+json itself because @RestControllerAdvice cannot see filter exceptions) and a malformed query parameter surfaces as MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException with its own handler; the sole production throw site is OperatorService.list for an out-of-range page (< 1).
B.fix: Reword the Javadoc to describe the real trigger (a request parameter that is syntactically valid but out of range, e.g. page < 1) and drop the missing-identity-header and malformed-query-param examples, so nobody throws this from a servlet filter expecting the advice to map it.

B.issue: The camelCase 'contract lock' test builds its own ObjectMapper and sets LOWER_CAMEL_CASE + failOnUnknownProperties(false) itself, so it asserts the strategy the test just configured, not the production JacksonConfig — deleting JacksonConfig entirely leaves this test green; the assertions are also presence-only (json.has) so a field serialising as null still passes
B.fix: Drop the hand-built mapper: either move this method into a @JsonTest/@SpringBootTest slice that injects the Spring-managed ObjectMapper (or applies JacksonConfig's Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer to a builder), and assert values not just key presence (json.get("addressLine1").asText() etc.); if the real-stack coverage in OperatorComplianceIT is deemed sufficient, delete this method rather than keep a tautology named as a contract lock

B.issue: request_deserialisesFromCamelCaseAndMapsOntoAnEntityIgnoringServerFields asserts entity.getOrganisationId() and entity.getStatus() are null under the comment 'Server-assigned fields in the body are ignored', but the JSON body carries neither an organisationId nor a status key — only id and deleted — so both assertions are unfalsifiable; no test in the repo posts an organisationId in a body, leaving the cv-010 tenant-smuggling guard entirely unexercised
B.fix: Add "organisationId": "OTHER-ORG", "status": "DELETED", "createdAt"/"modifiedAt" values to the body so the null assertions can actually fail, and add a matching AddressScopingIT case posting organisationId=ORG_B as ORG_A and asserting the persisted row is still ORG_A

B.issue: sampleEntity always populates all 14 fields, so no test ever maps an entity with the genuinely optional addressLine2/county absent, and none of OperatorResponse's 11 Objects.requireNonNull guards (id, name, addressLine1, townOrCity, postcode, countryCode, phone, email, organisationId, createdAt, modifiedAt) is exercised — a repo-wide grep for requireNonNull/NullPointerException/assertThatThrownBy/assertThrows in src/test returns nothing, so the deliberate fail-loud behaviour on a legacy or partially-written Mongo row is unpinned
B.fix: Add two cases: toResponse on an entity with null addressLine2 and null county maps cleanly (guards stay off the optional fields), and assertThatThrownBy(() -> operatorMapper.toResponse(entityWithNullPhone)).isInstanceOf(NullPointerException.class).hasMessage("phone") to pin at least one required-field guard

B.issue: Both tests are tautological: the declared return types are TimedAspect/CountedAspect, so isNotNull() plus isInstanceOf() can only fail if the factory returns null — nothing asserts the aspect was bound to the supplied MeterRegistry (pre-existing; this PR only changes the package line).
B.fix: Assert observable behaviour instead — e.g. exercise the aspect against a @Timed/@Counted proxy and assert the SimpleMeterRegistry records the meter, or drop the trivial tests and cover the beans via a @SpringBootTest/ApplicationContextRunner context assertion.

B.issue: Assertions pin camelCase wire names (jsonPath $.countryCode, $.organisationId, $.deleted) but the same PR commits docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml declaring snake_case (address_line_1, organisation_id, trace_id, country, telephone, status) — and docs/best-practices/rest-api/rest-api.md lists 'camelCase in JSON' under Don't. The compliance gate in OperatorComplianceIT only diffs path set, HTTP methods and operationIds against the locked contract, never schema properties, so this whole-model divergence ships untested. PR-wide issue, raised once here.
B.fix: Pick one authority: either regenerate/delete api-contract.locked.yaml so it matches the camelCase implementation, or move the implementation to snake_case; then extend the OperatorComplianceIT divergence gate to compare component schema property names, not just operationIds.

B.issue: getCrossOrgIdReturns404IdenticalToUnknownId is a near-verbatim duplicate of AddressScopingIT.a404ForAnotherOrgsLiveAddressIsByteIdenticalToA404ForAnUnknownId (same ORG_A/ORG_B/UNKNOWN_ID constants, same two requests, same problem-body equality) and assertThatProblemBodiesMatch duplicates AddressScopingIT.problemWithoutInstance. Both files are new in this PR, so the duplication is introduced here — two copies of a security-critical assertion will drift apart, and only one carries the comment explaining why instance is excluded.
B.fix: Delete the duplicate test from AddressGetIT and leave the cv-040 non-disclosure assertion in AddressScopingIT, which is the class that owns org scoping; or hoist the problem-body comparison helper into IntegrationBase and keep a single test.

B.issue: The happy-path GET asserts only 5 of the 14 OperatorResponse fields (id, name, countryCode, organisationId, deleted). The save() fixture seeds addressLine1, townOrCity, postcode, phone, email, createdAt and modifiedAt but none is asserted, so an OperatorMapper regression that drops or mis-maps any of them — including addressLine1, the exact field the two committed contract documents disagree about — passes this IT green. For the endpoint the class javadoc frames as the GET contract test, that is the wrong half of the payload pinned.
B.fix: Assert the remaining mapped fields on getLiveAddressReturns200WithDeletedFalse (addressLine1, townOrCity, postcode, phone, email, and createdAt/modifiedAt as exists()), or compare the whole body against an expected JSON document with content().json(...).

B.issue: save() seeds createdAt and modifiedAt with fixed Instants, but Address carries @CreatedDate/@LastModifiedDate and MongoConfig enables @EnableMongoAuditing, so repository.save() overwrites both with the current clock on insert. The seeded 2026-07-14T09:15:27Z values never reach the database and are never asserted — dead fixture that implies deterministic timestamps the test does not have.
B.fix: Drop the createdAt/modifiedAt builder calls from save(), or assert the auditing behaviour explicitly (e.g. read the saved entity back and assert the timestamps are non-null and were set by auditing rather than by the fixture).

B.issue: The class javadoc claims cross-org and unknown ids yield 'byte-identical 404s (cv-040)', but assertThatProblemBodiesMatch deserialises both bodies into a Map and removes the instance key before comparing — so neither byte identity, key order, nor the Content-Type header is actually asserted, and instance legitimately differs. AddressScopingIT documents the instance exclusion inline; this copy states a stronger guarantee than its own assertion provides.
B.fix: Reword the javadoc to 'identical problem bodies apart from the RFC 9457 instance, which echoes the caller own request URI', matching the comment already written in AddressScopingIT.

B.issue: The new primaryPreferred assertion is satisfied by the test profile's own copy of the property (src/test/resources/application-integration-test.yml:13 sets read-preference: primaryPreferred), so it does not lock the production default the comment claims to protect — reverting src/main/resources/application.yml:13 to 'secondary' leaves this test green.
B.fix: Delete the read-preference key from application-integration-test.yml so the integration-test profile inherits the main application.yml value, making this assertion a real regression guard on the production default.

B.issue: The test asserts only that the index is DECLARED (name + key order from listIndexes); it never runs an explain plan, so it cannot detect the failure it claims to guard - a declared index the planner does not actually choose for findByOrganisationIdAndStatus or the searchBy* $or/regex queries (COLLSCAN or in-memory SORT) still passes green.
B.fix: Add a behavioural assertion alongside the metadata one: run an explain (e.g. mongoTemplate.execute(db -> db.runCommand(new Document("explain", findCommand))) or Query with a real page+sort) for findByOrganisationIdAndStatus and assert winningPlan reaches an IXSCAN on indexName 'org_status_created' with no SORT stage.

B.issue: Cleanup is inline at the top of the test body instead of @BeforeEach, and the test then saves an all-null Address (builder().build(), no organisationId/status) that is never removed - it leaks into the shared 'addresses' collection of the shared Spring context/Mongo container for whatever IT class runs next; every sibling IT (AddressGetIT, AddressSearchIT, OperatorListIT etc.) only survives this because each happens to call deleteAll() in its own @BeforeEach.
B.fix: Move the deleteAll() into a @BeforeEach setUp() per the repo convention, and drop the save() entirely - auto-index-creation:true already creates the collection and index at context startup, so no document is needed to observe listIndexes.

B.issue: assertThat(indexNames).doesNotContain("crn_status_type_created", "org_status") is vacuous: neither name appears anywhere in the codebase (grep confirms only this line), the Mongo container is created fresh per run, and Spring's auto-index-creation only creates indexes declared on @Document classes - so no mechanism can ever put those names in the list and the assertion cannot fail. It reads as a migration guard against a stale deployed index, which a throwaway container structurally cannot see.
B.fix: Replace it with an exhaustive assertion that actually bites - assertThat(indexNames).containsExactlyInAnyOrder("_id_", "org_status_created") - which catches index bloat, renames and accidental extra @Indexed fields.

B.issue: The pin covers key names and key order but not sort directions: extracting(IndexField::getKey).containsExactly(...) passes unchanged if createdAt flips from -1 to 1 (or organisationId/status flip to -1), even though the class javadoc and Address.java both make 'newest-first' load-bearing. Flipping the whole def to descending would silently break Pageable sorts that the equality-prefix reverse scan cannot rescue.
B.fix: Extract the pair, e.g. .extracting(IndexField::getKey, IndexField::getDirection).containsExactly(tuple("organisationId", ASC), tuple("status", ASC), tuple("createdAt", DESC)), so the assertion matches the @CompoundIndex def exactly.

B.issue: The test omits the mandatory // Given // When // Then comment blocks that every other IT in this repo carries, and mongoTemplate.indexOps("addresses") hardcodes the collection name instead of deriving it from the entity, so a change to @Document(collection=...) on Address is not caught by the type system.
B.fix: Add the // Given // When // Then blocks per the repo IT convention, and use mongoTemplate.indexOps(Address.class) so the collection name is resolved from the @Document annotation.

B.issue: aPageSizeRequestParamIsNotHonouredTheServerConfigSizeApplies pins page_size as an ignored unknown query param, but the in-repo locked contract (docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml lines 124-132, 144) declares page_size as a supported query param (integer, min 1, max 100, default 25) and specifies 400 when it is out of range; the cited ruling 'cv-025' appears nowhere in the repo except this test and the two javadocs that assert it, so the only in-repo authority contradicts the test. A contract-conformant client sending page_size=50 silently gets 25 back with no error, and this test locks that in.
B.fix: Resolve the conflict before merge: either implement page_size as a bound @RequestParam (default 25, 1..100, 400 outside) and rewrite this test to assert page_size=5 returns 5 items, or amend the locked contract to drop the page_size parameter under a recorded ruling and cite that ruling in the test comment. Note the current test only exercises Spring MVC's default 'ignore unknown params' behaviour, not any code in this repo.

B.issue: Page metadata is asserted camelCase ($.pageSize, $.totalItems, $.totalPages at lines 75-77, 89-90, 101, 115, 146-147) but the in-repo locked contract's OperatorPage schema (docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml lines 589-614) requires page_size, total_items and total_pages, and the contract header calls itself LOCKED with 'nothing in M1/M2/M3 may change this file'. OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate only compares paths, HTTP methods and operationIds, so nothing detects this property-name drift - this IT is one of the places that cements it.
B.fix: Get the camelCase-vs-snake_case ruling recorded, then make the two sides agree: either regenerate api-contract.locked.yaml to camelCase and re-assert here, or serialise the page record snake_case and change these assertions. Whichever way it goes, extend OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate to compare schema property names so drift fails the build instead of being pinned by tests.

B.issue: The class javadoc says the IT pins a 'newest-first' listing, but no test asserts ordering, and listPageTwoReturnsTheRemaining5 only asserts items.length()==5 - never that page 2 holds the 5 addresses page 1 did not. Pagination could return an overlapping or entirely wrong 5-item window, or the createdAt DESC sort could be lost, and every assertion in this class still passes. OperatorServiceTest only captures the Pageable sort spec against a mocked repository, so nothing proves Mongo actually serves newest-first via the org_status_created index.
B.fix: Give the seeds distinct, controlled createdAt values, then assert the concrete order (e.g. items[0].name is the newest) and collect the ids from page 1 and page 2 and assert the two sets are disjoint and together cover all 30.

B.issue: save() sets .createdAt(Instant.parse("2026-07-14T09:15:27Z")) and the same .modifiedAt on every seeded Address, but Address carries @CreatedDate/@LastModifiedDate and MongoConfig is annotated @EnableMongoAuditing, so on insert (id null, entity is new) Spring Data's auditing handler overwrites both with now(). The fixture values are inert; a maintainer reading them will believe the sort key is controlled and identical across all 30 rows when in fact it is wall-clock insert time.
B.fix: Drop the .createdAt/.modifiedAt builder calls, or - if the fix for the ordering gap needs controlled timestamps - set them by re-saving the persisted entity (auditing does not re-stamp @CreatedDate on an existing document) or by writing through MongoTemplate, and add a comment stating why.

B.issue: Page-boundary coverage stops at page 0. There is no test for a page beyond the last (e.g. page=3 with 30 seeded addresses) - the boundary a paginated UI hits first via a stale bookmark, a browser back button, or a delete that shrinks the result set under a user sitting on the last page. Neither the locked contract nor OperatorService.list defines that behaviour (page >= 1 passes the guard, so Mongo returns an empty page: 200 with items [] but page 3 and totalPages 2), and a negative page is likewise untested. The frontend has no pinned answer to build against.
B.fix: Add a test for page beyond the last asserting the agreed shape (200 with empty items, page echoed, totalItems 30, totalPages 2 - or a 400 if that is the ruling), and add a negative page case to the existing page-0 test as a parameterised @ValueSource of "0" and "-1".

B.issue: Test method names do not follow the prescribed {subject}_{shouldDoWhat}[_{whenContext}] convention (e.g. listDefaultsToPage1Size25AndReportsTotalPages2For30Addresses instead of list_shouldReturn25ItemsAcross2Pages_when30Addresses), and no test carries the required explicit // Given, // When, // Then comment blocks, which integration.md states must be present even when When and Then are combined in a fluent chain.
B.fix: Rename the eight test methods to the subject_shouldDoWhat_whenContext form and add the Given/When/Then comment blocks, applying the same change across the sibling ITs added in this PR so the repo lands on one convention.
